description: Hey! We're Faraza and VYLT, two longtime friends and high school students who share an interest in space and technology. Faraza is the outgoing team leader who enjoys researching, presenting ideas, and working with AI, while VYLT is the creative mind behind our coding and design work. We balance each other out and love turning ideas into reality. We're looking for friendly, creative people with different skills who already know their way around AI!
summary: Terraphone is an interactive web project that transforms NASA Earth-observation data into experiences combining visualization, sound, and gameplay. Its Global Rain module presents precipitation on a 3D globe and pairs it with rain, storm, and habitat-inspired soundscapes. The Sound of Change lets users explore how urban-policy choices could affect modeled city noise, with visual and audio feedback. Earth Arcade offers six mini-games inspired by NASA missions and datasets, covering topics such as wildfires, urban heat, clouds, ozone, coral reefs, and forests. Together, the modules invite users to explore environmental data in an accessible, multisensory way.
details:
Terraphone is an interactive web project that makes Earth and environmental data engaging through sound, visualization, simulation, and games. It has three main sections: Global Rain, which displays NASA precipitation data on a 3D globe with a soundscape; The Sound of Change, which lets users explore how urban-noise interventions may affect modeled sound levels; and Earth Arcade, a collection of six environmental mini-games inspired by NASA missions and datasets.

The project aims to make complex environmental topics easier to explore and encourage interest in Earth science and possible solutions. Its creative approach combines data with audio, interactive controls, and gameplay. While designing it, we considered how to make the experiences understandable and engaging, and how to distinguish simulations and games from direct real-world measurements.

Terraphone was built with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, using native web technologies including ES Modules, the Web Audio API, WebGL with MapLibre GL, and HTML5 Canvas. It draws on NASA data and references, as well as guidance from organizations including WHO and UNEP.
